title: Token Context Inspector & Composable Metrics Grid — Figma library and consistency review
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a focused Figma library and interaction spec for two related console patterns: (1) a Token Context Inspector panel that surfaces which design tokens (spacing, color, elevation, density) are active for any selected console surface and shows their provenance and recommended fallbacks; and (2) a Composable Metrics Grid — a responsive grid of small, embeddable metric widgets that can be composed into dashboards and rollout pages. Goal is to standardize token usage across dashboard/rollout screens, reduce visual drift, and enable quicker design-to-engine handoffs.

Background: Multiple console pages have diverged on spacing, chip states, and headline sizing — especially within rollout and cost views where small density differences cascade into layout regressions. Platform engineers need a clear mapping from visual components to token families and exportable Figma components with named variants to drive the runtime prop/slot model. This ticket creates an inspector and grid spec to bridge design, product and engineering.

Outcomes:
- Deliver a Figma library file with Token Context Inspector components, Token provenance flyout, and the Composable Metrics Grid component set plus documented variants.
- Provide an interaction spec for how the inspector is invoked from any console surface (right-click / inspect mode) and how metrics grid cells adapt across breakpoints.
- Produce a single consistency checklist (PDF/Confluence) for use in design reviews and engineering PR templates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma library published and linked, with clear component naming conventions (token.family.tokenName) and at least 6 grid cell variants (metric, sparkline, status-pill, cost-summary, compare-previous, hover-detail).
- Token Context Inspector: shows active tokens, token source (global, component, local override), suggested fallback tokens, and an exportable snippet for engineers (token keys + current resolved values).
- Interaction flows documented: open inspector, highlight affected elements, copy token set, and quick-create component variant from selection.
- Accessibility annotations: contrast checks for all widget variants and keyboard shortcuts for inspector nav.
- Design review signoff from PM (Daniel Cho) and Eng lead (Liam O'Connor).
design_notes: Prefer canonical token names (color.surface-1, spacing-xxs) to ambiguous labels — reduces implementation mismatch.
Inspector should avoid heavy chrome; use translucent overlay and outline to keep context visible.
Grid cells must be isolated components with a single API surface: title, value, trend, helper, statusBadge, actions.
Default grid layout: 12-column responsive with breakpoints at 1280px and 720px. Cells can span 3/6/12 columns.
Provide an opt-in dense mode token that adjusts vertical rhythm and font sizes for high-information dashboards.
decisions: Use token provenance model: global -> component -> local override (display all three where present).
Expose token keys as kebab-case string for easy copy/paste into runtime config and SDK mapping.
Implement inspector UX as a transient overlay in Figma with an optional persistent panel for deep inspection.
Grid component API chosen to match frontend props (size, variant, compact, showTrend, onClick) to simplify handoff.
tradeoffs: Showing full token provenance increases complexity in the inspector UI but reduces ambiguity for engineers.
Dense mode improves information density but risks micro-contrast issues; mitigations included in accessibility checks.
Creating many grid cell variants increases design maintenance burden; we limited to 6 core variants to balance coverage and upkeep.
review_feedback: PM Daniel Cho: prioritize cost-summary and compare-previous variants for rollout pages — flagged as critical for Q2 metrics features.
Eng Liam O'Connor: request for token export format to include hex + computed rgba for transparency layers — added to acceptance criteria.
Accessibility (Sophie Wang): run automated contrast check and provide manual notes for badge colors in dark mode.
Design Director (Maria Fernandez): prefer single source Figma file with component library and separate example playground page.
